newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs end mildly higher.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs end mildly higher.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts finished slightly higher in quiet trade on Wednesday, after local Indian stocks were again hit by profit-taking earlier, traders said.
They said the market was consolidating following recent volatility and the resolution of the country's political crisis.

New Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Tuesday won a confidence vote in parliament as expected and traders said that with political stability, the market was now likely to focus on corporate results.
Also, they said GDRs had risen ahead of the local market before the weekend, and this week were correcting to more sustainable levels.
As a result, GDR prices were seen capped by a relatively sluggish local market.
Reliance shed 37 cents to $18.50/$19.50, SBI made 40 cents to $24.00/$25.00 and VSNL picked up 20 cents to $19.80/20.30.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.26 points, or 0.32 percent, up at 79.80, with the premium over the local market at 18.88 percent from 19.73 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index added 28.36 points to 3,828.99.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 1.97 points to 128.43, representing a discount to the local market of 3.41 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 1.23 points, or 1.95 percent, up at 64.57, a premium of 34.31 percent over the local market.
